units.text: The Evidence Map: What We Know and What Does Not Follow

This map summarizes the status of inferences rather than repeating every finding. Numbers lead to bibliography sources. Papers published in 2026 are included with the status available when research for the book was completed.
Play, Curiosity, and Generation

Studies on uncertainty and curiosity [1] [2] . Support mechanisms and effects under bounded experimental conditions. They do not establish a universal proportion of chance that maximizes pleasure or demonstrate dependence on LLMs.
Near miss [5] . Subjective effects and behavioral persistence are not the same measure. Transfer to the “semantic near miss” remains a hypothesis of the book.
Generation and aggregation [6] [7] . Show the importance of how answers are produced and selected. They do not give the majority the status of independent evidence.
Beliefs and Mental Health
Sycophancy [8] [9] . Experimental research exists on excessive agreement and certain effects on judgment. These findings are not equivalent to a clinical diagnosis.
The Bayesian model [10] . A demonstration within a theoretical model, not an epidemiological estimate.
The clinical case [13] . Documents a complex real situation. It does not isolate a sole cause or provide the population risk rate.
The 185 accounts [14] . A preliminary signal from a self-selected sample. Its proportions cannot be extended to all users.
Affective use [16] . Combines methods with different causal powers. The effect of voluntary usage duration must not be confused with the effect of the randomized condition.
SIM-VAIL [17] . Evaluates simulated conversations through a clinically validated framework. It does not measure symptom onset in patients exposed in real life.
Provider indicators [45] . Estimates of conversational signals, not diagnoses or cases causally attributed to the chatbot.
Work and Skills
Productivity experiments [19] [20] . Results can differ between tasks and contexts without contradicting one another. No percentage is a universal speed multiplier.
The meta-analysis [21] . The average effect does not eliminate heterogeneity. Lack of significance does not prove the absence of every educational effect.
METR update and survey [22] [23] . Changes in participant selection complicate measurement; self-assessed value is not independently measured value.
Organizational experiences [24] [25] [28] [29] . Help reveal new tasks and transferred costs. Samples and methods limit generalization.
Critical thinking [27] . The survey does not demonstrate permanent cognitive decline. The operational question is which skills are practiced and how they are evaluated.
Correctness and Interventions
Evaluation of texts and code [30] [31] [32] [37] . A benchmark measures part of the task. Coverage, provenance, and relevance must be checked separately.
Judges and self-correction [33] [34] [35] . External feedback can matter more than new wording. No critic model is infallible.
Interface interventions [36] [43] . Can reduce certain forms of overreliance in tested contexts. They are not clinical treatments.
Proofs and security [38] [39] [40] [41] . The strength of the guarantee depends on the property, assumptions, and environment. Protecting the evaluator is part of the system, not an external detail.
